Subject: Clarification: how billing rounds for very long-context / multi-call flows

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — procurement wants one more clarity point before we finalize numbers for the renewal. Two short scenarios below that our accounting team flagged when they modeled costs:

1) A single API call that submits a 70k-token system+history context and requests a 3k-token completion. How is that billed (unitization + rounding)?
2) A hybrid UX where the UI streams incremental user messages every 30s (each ~200 tokens) but we keep a retained prefix of ~48k tokens in a KV cache across the session. We might have 50 calls in a day for a single user. Does prefix retention reduce per-call billing? Any minimums applied per-call or per-session?

We modeled two options and the delta is material to our forecast. If you can send the exact rounding rules and a sample invoice line for both scenarios that would help procurement and our finance partner sign off.

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear scenarios. I pulled Camila (SE) and Tessa (sales ops/finance) in so we can give exact lines you can put on your forecast. Summary up front, then a worked example + attachments with a sample invoice and token spreadsheet.

High-level principles (short):
- Token accounting: we bill actual tokens consumed, but apply a two-tier rounding rule that reduces invoice noise for short calls while keeping long-context accuracy.
- Rounding rule: Calls with total billed tokens <= 4,000 are rounded up to the nearest 50 tokens. Calls > 4,000 tokens use 1,000-token granularity for rounding. This is intended to reduce volatility from micro-calls while keeping larger calls precise.
- Prefix / KV caching: retained prefix tokens are only billed when they are included in the request sent to the model. For sticky cached prefixes we credit repeated full-prefix replays via a prefix-reuse rebate (visible as a negative line on invoice when hit).
- Session minimums: we do not apply a per-session minimum; minimums apply per-invoice line only for certain pilot SKUs (not applicable here).

Worked examples (attached as token-accounting-sample.xlsx):
A) Single-call long-context: 70,000 context + 3,000 completion = 73,000 billed tokens -> rounding applied at 1,000-token granularity -> billed tokens = 73,000 (already multiple of 1,000? If not, round up, e.g., 73,124 -> 74,000). Example invoice line in attachment shows unit price and resulting cost.

B) Hybrid streaming + cached prefix: request includes retained prefix 48,000 + incremental user chunk 200 + completion 300 = 48,500 tokens per call. Rounding: >4,000 so 1,000-token granularity -> each call billed at 49,000 tokens. If you make 50 such calls and we detect prefix cache reuse across calls, you may see a prefix-reuse rebate applied as a separate credit line that subtracts the repeated-prefix portion after the first full charge. The rebate is applied when prefix reuse is over the detection threshold (configurable per account).

Files attached: sample-invoice-BrightCart-Q3.pdf, token-accounting-sample.xlsx (with per-scenario math).

If it helps, Camila can provide the short explainer you can hand to your controller.

Best,

Sergio / Tessa — quick operational notes to confirm before I send an internal explainer to BrightCart:

- The rounding that Sergio described is intentional to keep invoices readable. Implementation details: we compute raw token_count per request (context + input + completion). If token_count <= 4000 -> ceil(token_count / 50) * 50; else -> ceil(token_count / 1000) * 1000. This is done at the request level before rate multipliers / discounts.
- Prefix-reuse rebate: triggered when identical prefix hash appears in >3 calls within an invoice period. The rebate amount equals the lesser of repeated-prefix-tokens * unit_price and a monthly cap tied to the account tier. We should be explicit on BrightCart's tier — looks like they are in Enterprise Standard (no pilot SKUs).
- Discounts and committed-volume: discounts apply after rounding. For BrightCart's committed discount (15% at $400k ARR), the discount multiplier is applied to the rounded token charge. This means rounding can slightly shift discount value in dollar terms (small rounding delta).

Question for Tessa / Kimberly: any reason not to document the prefix-reuse threshold at >3 calls? Legal asked about gaming risk; we have fraud protections, but we should make the trigger conservative.

I'll draft a one-pager with the worked numbers and a sample invoice line for both scenarios.
